Formerly it went on from Robertsbridge past Appledore and Ruckinge to the Channel at Lympne. The fact that places with names such as Nympton are to be found both on the Yeo and the Mole does not indicate, as suggested by Napier & Stevenson, Crawford 58 ff., that Nymet was originally a name of a forest, for the Mole was demonstrably known as Nimet in the 13th century, and there is nothing remarkable in the fact that two streams not far apart have the same name.
